title: Arizona Chip Journey
subtitle: How a chip takes shape in Arizona.
html:
Open Arizona Chip Journey ↗

Understand Arizona through the manufacturing process

Arizona Chip Journey connects semiconductor process explanations, material and equipment functions, Arizona locations, and public sources. Readers can move from what a step does to the resources it requires and the local nodes worth researching further.

Content structure

A wafer-production prelude covers polysilicon, crystal growth, slicing, polishing, and inspection before fab entry.

Six process chapters: Wafer Start & Surface Preparation → Patterning & Layer Transfer → Device Formation → Contacts & Interconnect → Wafer Test & Yield → Advanced Packaging & Final Test.

The chapters connect process explanations with material and equipment functions, companies, Arizona nodes, and traceable public sources. Water, gases, chemicals, facilities, and logistics are treated as support across stages.

Connect the process to places and the wider system

Arizona Innovation Map provides the location view. Ecosystem Network provides the sector and support-layer view. Together, the three entry points organize the research by process, geography, and system structure.

How to interpret the project

The six chapters are an educational structure used by this project. Manufacturing includes repeated process cycles; company research also needs to distinguish public capabilities, local presence, and commercial relationships supported by evidence.
